no_account.text: Counter 1. I can't take a slip without an account — Ines at Account Opening opens them, the desk with the plant.

why_no_account.text: Every payment here is executed by your own account contract. Until it's cloned and initialised there is nothing for me to stamp.

idle.text: Counter 1. Paying someone? Up to {limit} {symbol} I do right here; more than that goes through the vault.

payees.text: Anyone with an address — the florist, the landlord, the demo merchant are on the slip. What's actually approved on your account is the demo token for the transfer service; that's the list on my wall.

why_payees.text: The guard whitelist is per function selector: your account may call transfer on the demo token and nothing else. Payee addresses are parameters inside that call, so they are not whitelisted individually.

services.text: Two services at this counter: a payment over the counter, done in one step, and a scheduled wire, which goes into the vault for {timelock} before anyone can release it.

why_services.text: Over the counter is requestAndApproveExecution — request and approval in one transaction, which is why there is no wait. A wire is executeWithTimeLock — a PENDING record with a releaseTime — then approveTimeLockExecution or cancelTimeLockExecution later.

why_counter.text: You sign the slip; I execute it. That's a meta-transaction: your signature authorises, my desk pays the gas and submits. Within your instant limit it's approved and executed in one step.

pay_now.text: {amount} {symbol} to {payee}. Over the counter — one moment.

paid.text: Done. Here's your receipt: {amount} {symbol} to {payee}, record #{txId}. Balance now {balance} {symbol}.

why_instant.text: Executed by the Teller under your signed instruction — a meta-transaction: the session signer signed the EIP-712 slip for your account, the broadcaster submitted requestAndApproveExecution, and the transfer ran inside your own contract. The receipt's fine print is the transaction hash {hash}.

over_limit.text: {amount} {symbol} — that's above what I can do here. It goes through the vault: a cooling period of {timelock}, then it needs a release. Walk with me.

choices.working: Filing your wire with the vault…

why_vault_route.text: Large movements are requested now and executed later. Between the two, you or the manager can recall it. It's the same account, just a slower lane — and the instant limit itself is branch policy, enforced at my desk; on chain the real controls are the guards and which actions your roles hold.

wired.text: Filed. Wire #{txId} is in the vault; it releases in {release_in}. Ruth at the vault window releases it once the clock runs down — or Mr. Okafor can skip the cooling if you bring a hand scan, or recall it.

why_wired.text: That was your own transaction — executeWithTimeLock, signed inside the enclave by the session signer under a policy pinned to your account, broadcast by this desk. The record's releaseTime is set by the contract; the wall clock reads it back.
